title.zh: 卷六十八 唐書44: 列傳20 薛廷珪 崔沂 劉岳 封舜卿 竇夢徵 李保殷 歸藹 孔邈 張文寶 陳乂 劉贊
title.en: Volume 68 Book of Later Tang 44: Biographies 20: Xue Tinggui, Cui Yi, Liu Yue, Liu Ye, Feng Shunqing, Dou Mengzheng, Li Baoyin, Gui Ai, Kong, Miao, Zhang Wenbao, Chen Yi, Liu Zan
title.raw: 卷六十八 唐書44: 列傳20 薛廷珪 崔沂 劉岳 封舜卿 竇夢徵 李保殷 歸藹 孔邈 張文寶 陳乂 劉贊 Volume 68 Book of Later Tang 44: Biographies 20: Xue Tinggui, Cui Yi, Liu Yue, Liu Ye, Feng Shunqing, Dou Mengzheng, Li Baoyin, Gui Ai, Kong, Miao, Zhang Wenbao, Chen Yi, Liu Zan

sentences.zh: 薛廷珪，其先河東人也。

translations.literal: Xue Tinggui — his ancestors were people of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Tinggui came of a Hedong family.

sentences.zh: 父逢，咸通中為秘書監，以才名著於時。

translations.literal: His father Feng, during the Xiantong reign period served as Director of the Palace Library, and was renowned in his time for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feng served as Director of the Palace Library under Emperor Yizong and was widely celebrated for his gifts as a writer.

sentences.zh: 廷珪，中和年在西川登進士第，累曆台省。

translations.literal: Tinggui, in the Zhonghe years passed the jinshi examination in Xichuan, and successively held posts in the central secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui earned his jinshi degree in Sichuan during the Zhonghe era and rose through a series of central-government posts.

sentences.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：大順初，累遷司勳員外郎、知制誥。）〉

translations.literal: (Old Book of Tang: At the beginning of the Dashun reign he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Merit and to Drafting Commissioner.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (According to the Old Book of Tang, in early Dashun he was promoted in succession to Vice Director in the Bureau of Merit and commissioner for drafting imperial edicts.)〉

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，為中書舍人。

translations.literal: During Qianning, he was a Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianning era he served as a drafting secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 駕在華州，改散騎常侍，尋請致仕，客遊蜀川。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Huazhou, he was reassigned as Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; soon he requested retirement from office and traveled as a guest in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was at Huazhou he was made Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, then soon asked to retire and lived for a time as a guest in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遷洛陽，征為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, he was summoned as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong relocated to Luoyang, Tinggui was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：光化中，復為中書舍人，遷邢部、吏部二侍郎，權知禮部貢舉，拜尚書左丞。）〉

translations.literal: (Old Book of Tang: In Guanghua he again became Secretariat Drafting Secretary, was promoted to Vice Ministers of Punishments and of Personnel, acted as provisional overseer of the Ministry of Rites examination, and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Old Book of Tang adds that in the Guanghua era he again became a Secretariat drafting secretary, rose to vice minister of punishments and of personnel, temporarily supervised the civil-service examinations for the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉

sentences.zh: 時柳璨屠害朝士，衣冠畢罹其毒，廷珪以居常退讓獲全。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Can slaughtered court officials; the gentry all suffered his poison, but Tinggui was spared because of his usual modesty and yielding conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Can was butchering court officials, the entire official class fell victim to him; Tinggui alone escaped harm through his habitual modesty and restraint.

sentences.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：朱全忠兼四鎮，廷珪以官告使至汴，客將先見，諷其拜。

translations.literal: (New Book of Tang: Zhu Quanzhong held four circuits concurrently; Tinggui arrived at Bian as commissioner bearing the patent of office, and a guest officer who met him first hinted that he should bow.
translations.idiomatic: (The New Book of Tang records that when Zhu Quanzhong held four military circuits at once, Tinggui came to Bian as the bearer of his commission of office. A host officer received him first and suggested obliquely that he should bow.

sentences.zh: 廷珪佯不曉，曰：「吾何德，敢受令公拜乎！」

translations.literal: Tinggui pretended not to understand, saying: "What virtue do I have, that I dare receive the Lord Commander's bow!"
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui feigned not to understand and said, "What merit have I that I should accept a bow from Your Lordship!"

sentences.zh: 及見，卒不肯加禮。）〉

translations.literal: When they met, he in the end refused to add the courtesy.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When they met face to face, he still refused to offer the courtesy.)〉

sentences.zh: 入梁為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Entering Liang service, he became Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he became Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平定河南，以廷珪年老，除太子少師致仕。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Henan, because Tinggui was old he was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent with junior third rank and retired.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong pacified Henan, Tinggui was granted retirement as Mentor of the Heir Apparent on account of his advanced age.

sentences.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：廷珪與李琪嘗為太祖冊禮使。）〉

translations.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Tinggui and Li Qi once served as enfeoffment ritual commissioners for Taizu.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian notes that Tinggui and Li Qi had once served together as ritual commissioners for Taizu's investiture.)〉

sentences.zh: 同光三年九月卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Tongguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Tongguang 3 (925).

sentences.zh: 贈右僕射。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 所著《鳳閣詞書》十卷、《克家志》五卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: His works Phoenix Pavilion Literary Writings in ten fascicles and Record of Honoring the Family in five fascicles both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works Phoenix Pavilion Literary Writings, in ten fascicles, and Record of Honoring the Family, in five fascicles, both circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 初，廷珪父逢，著《鑿混沌》、《真珠簾》等賦，大為時人所稱。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tinggui's father Feng had composed rhapsodies such as Boring Through Chaos and Pearl Curtain, which were greatly praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui's father Feng had earlier written celebrated rhapsodies such as Boring Through Chaos and Pearl Curtain that won wide praise in their day.

sentences.zh: 廷珪既壯，亦著賦數十篇，同為一集，故目曰《克家志》。

translations.literal: When Tinggui reached maturity, he also composed several dozen rhapsodies, gathered into one collection, hence its title Record of Honoring the Family.
translations.idiomatic: When Tinggui came of age he too wrote several dozen rhapsodies and collected them in one volume, which he titled Record of Honoring the Family.

sentences.zh: 崔沂，

translations.literal: Cui Yi,
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yi,

sentences.zh: 〈（《新唐書·宰相世係表》：沂，字德潤。）〉

translations.literal: (New Book of Tang, Genealogical Tables of Chief Ministers: Yi, style name Derun.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The New Book of Tang's tables of chief ministers give his style name as Derun.)〉

sentences.zh: 大中時宰相魏公鉉之幼子也。

translations.literal: He was the youngest son of Grand Councilor Duke of Wei Gongxuan of the Dazhong era.
translations.idiomatic: He was the youngest son of Wei Gongxuan, Duke of Wei, who had served as chief councilor under Emperor Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 兄沆，廣明初亦為宰輔。

translations.literal: His elder brother Hong, at the beginning of Guangming also became a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Hong likewise reached the chief ministership early in the Guangming era.

sentences.zh: 沂舉進士第，曆監察、補闕。

translations.literal: Yi passed the jinshi examination and successively served as Investigating Censor and Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Yi passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as investigating censor and remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 昭宗時，累遷至員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: During Zhaozong's reign he was repeatedly promoted to Outer Court Director and Drafting Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaozong he rose in stages to outer-court director and drafting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 性抗厲守道，而文藻非優，嘗與同舍顏蕘、錢珝俱秉筆，見蕘、珝贍速，草制數十，無妨譚笑，而沂自愧。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and upheld the Way, but his literary polish was not superior; once he drafted together with colleagues Yan Rao and Qian Pei, and seeing Rao and Pei swift and ample, drafting several dozen edicts without hindering banter, Yi felt ashamed of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Firm and principled by nature, he was not a gifted stylist. Once, drafting edicts alongside colleagues Yan Rao and Qian Pei, he watched them turn out dozens of documents with ease, chatting and laughing all the while, and was mortified by his own slowness.

sentences.zh: 翌日，謁國相訴曰：「沂疏淺，不足以供詞翰之職。」

translations.literal: The next day he called on the chief minister and pleaded: "Yi is shallow and insufficient to fulfill the duties of literary drafting."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he called on the chief minister and said, "I am too shallow a writer to hold a drafting post."

sentences.zh: 相輔然之，移為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: The minister agreed and transferred him to Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The minister concurred and moved him to the post of grand censor.

sentences.zh: 入梁，為御史司憲，糾繆繩違，不避豪右。

translations.literal: Entering Liang service, he became Director of the Censorate, correcting errors and restraining violations, not avoiding powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he headed the Censorate, correcting abuses and enforcing the law without fear of the powerful.

sentences.zh: 開平中，金吾街使寇彥卿入朝，過天津橋，市民梁現者不時回避，前導伍伯捽之，投石欄以致斃。

translations.literal: During Kaiping, Jinwu Street Commissioner Kou Yanqing entered court audience, passed Tianjin Bridge, and a townsman named Liang Xian failed to withdraw in time; the forward escort guards seized him and threw him against a stone railing, causing death.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiping, Jinwu street commissioner Kou Yanqing came to court and crossed Tianjin Bridge. A townsman named Liang Xian failed to clear the way in time; Kou's escort guards seized him and hurled him against a stone railing, killing him.

sentences.zh: 彥卿自前白於梁祖，梁祖命通事舍人趙可封宣諭，令出私財與死者之家，以贖其罪。

translations.literal: Yanqing himself went forward to report to the Liang founder; the founder ordered Palace Usher Zhao Kefeng to announce the instruction, directing him to pay private funds to the dead man's family to redeem his offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing reported the matter himself to the Liang founder, who ordered palace usher Zhao Kefeng to announce that Yanqing should pay compensation from his private funds to the victim's family in lieu of punishment.

sentences.zh: 沂奏劾曰：「彥卿位是人臣，無專殺之理。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized in impeachment: "Yanqing's position is that of a subject; there is no principle of unauthorized killing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted an impeachment memorial: "Yanqing is a subject of the throne and has no right to kill on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 況天津橋御路之要，正對端門，當車駕出入之途，非街使震怒之所。

translations.literal: Moreover Tianjin Bridge is a vital point on the imperial roadway, directly facing the Gate of Propriety, on the route of the imperial carriage's coming and going — not a place for a street commissioner to vent rage.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Tianjin Bridge lies on the main imperial thoroughfare, directly before the Gate of Propriety, on the very path the imperial carriage takes; it is no place for a street commissioner to vent his anger.

sentences.zh: 況梁現不時回避，其過止於鞭笞。

translations.literal: Moreover Liang Xian's failure to withdraw in time — his offense goes no further than flogging.
translations.idiomatic: As for Liang Xian's failure to clear the way in time, the offense warranted no more than a beating.

sentences.zh: 捽首投驅，深乖朝憲，請論之以法。」

translations.literal: Seizing him by the head and casting him to death deeply violates court statutes; I request that he be judged by law."
translations.idiomatic: To seize a man and dash him to death so flagrantly violates the statutes; I ask that he be prosecuted according to law."

sentences.zh: 梁祖惜彥卿，令沂以過失論，沂引鬥競律，以怙勢力為罪首，下手者減一等。

translations.literal: The Liang founder valued Yanqing and ordered Yi to judge it as a case of negligence; Yi cited the statute on brawling, making reliance on power the chief offense and reducing one degree for those who carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang founder was reluctant to punish Yanqing and told Yi to treat the case as negligence. Yi cited the statute on brawling, naming abuse of power as the principal offense and reducing the penalty by one degree for those who carried out the act.

sentences.zh: 又鬥毆條，不鬥故毆傷人者，加傷罪一等。

translations.literal: He also cited the article on fighting: one who without fighting deliberately beats and injures a person has the injury offense increased by one degree.
translations.idiomatic: He also invoked the article on assault: anyone who, without a prior fight, deliberately beats and injures another has the injury charge increased by one degree.

sentences.zh: 沂表入，責授彥卿遊擊將軍、左衛中郎將。

translations.literal: When Yi's memorial entered, Yanqing was demoted and appointed General of the Patrol and Middle General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi's memorial was received, Yanqing was demoted to general of the patrol and middle general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 沂剛正守法，人士多之。

translations.literal: Yi was upright and upheld the law; scholars and officials greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's stern integrity in upholding the law won him wide admiration among the official class.

sentences.zh: 遷左司侍郎，改太常卿，轉禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Left Secretariat, changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the left secretariat, then made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and later minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 貞明中，帶本官充西京副留守。

translations.literal: During Zhenming, while retaining his original office he served as Deputy Protector-General of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenming he served as deputy protector-general of the Western Capital while retaining his ministerial title.

sentences.zh: 時張全義留守、天下兵馬副元帥、河南尹、判六軍諸衛事、守太尉、中書令、魏王，名位之重，冠絕中外。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Quanyi was Protector-General, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven, Prefect of Henan, Controller of the Six Armies and All Guards, Acting Grand Preceptor, Grand Secretariat Director, and Prince of Wei — the weight of his titles and position surpassed all within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi then held the posts of protector-general, deputy commander-in-chief of all forces, prefect of Henan, controller of the six armies and all guards, acting grand preceptor, grand secretariat director, and Prince of Wei — titles whose weight surpassed every other figure at court or in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 沂至府，客將白以副留守合行廷禮，沂曰：「張公官位至重，然尚帶府尹之名，不知副留守見尹之儀何如？」

translations.literal: When Yi arrived at the headquarters, a guest officer reported that as deputy protector he ought to perform court ritual; Yi said: "Lord Zhang's office and rank are extremely weighty, yet he still bears the title of prefect — I do not know what ceremony the deputy protector should use in meeting the prefect."
translations.idiomatic: When Yi arrived at headquarters, a staff officer told him that as deputy protector he was expected to perform court ceremony. Yi replied, "Lord Zhang's rank is immense, yet he still holds the title of prefect — I am not sure what protocol a deputy protector should follow in meeting a prefect?"

sentences.zh: 全義知之，遽引見沂，勞曰：「彼此有禮，俱老矣，勿相勞煩。」

translations.literal: Quanyi learned of this, hurriedly received Yi in audience, and comforted him: "Between us there is mutual courtesy; we are both old — do not trouble each other with formalities."
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi heard of this, summoned Yi at once, and said kindly, "Let us observe courtesy between equals — we are both old men; spare each other the formalities."

sentences.zh: 莊宗興復唐室，復用為左丞，判吏部尚書銓選司，坐累謫石州司馬。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong restored the Tang house, Yi was again employed as Left Vice Director, concurrently overseeing the Ministry of Personnel selection bureau; through accumulated offenses he was demoted to Defender of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong restored the Tang, Yi was again appointed left vice director and placed in charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection bureau; he was later demoted to defender of Shizhou on accumulated charges.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，召還，復為左丞。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he was recalled and again made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong came to the throne, Yi was recalled and restored as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 以衰疾告老，授太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: Because of age and illness he requested retirement and was granted Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Citing age and illness, he petitioned to retire and was granted the post of junior mentor of the heir apparent with retirement honors.

sentences.zh: 卒於龍門之別墅，時年七十餘。

translations.literal: He died at a villa in Longmen, aged over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his villa in Longmen at over seventy years of age.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 劉岳，字昭輔。

translations.literal: Liu Yue, style name Zhaofu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue, whose style was Zhaofu.

sentences.zh: 其先遼東襄平人，元魏平定遼東，徙家於代，隨孝文遷洛，遂為洛陽人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were people of Xiangping in Liaodong; when Northern Wei pacified Liaodong the family moved to Dai, followed Emperor Xiaowen in the move to Luoyang, and thus became Luoyang people.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears came from Xiangping in Liaodong. When the Northern Wei pacified the northeast the family was moved to Dai; they followed Emperor Xiaowen to Luoyang and became Luoyang natives.

sentences.zh: 八代祖民部尚書渝國公政會，武德時功臣。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Zhenghui, Minister of the Household and Duke of Yu of the Yu State, was a meritorious minister of the Wude era.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations back stood Zhenghui, minister of the household and Duke of Yu, a founding merit-holder of the Wude era.

sentences.zh: 祖符，蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fu was Prefect of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fu had been prefect of Cai.

sentences.zh: 父珪，洪洞縣令。

translations.literal: His father Gui was Magistrate of Hongtong County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui served as magistrate of Hongtong County.

sentences.zh: 符有子八人，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: Fu had eight sons, all of whom passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had eight sons, every one of whom passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 珪之母弟瑰、玕，異母弟崇夷、崇龜、崇望、崇魯、崇謨。

translations.literal: Gui the father's younger brothers by the same mother were Kui and Gan; younger brothers by a different mother were Chongyi, Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo.
translations.idiomatic: The father Gui's full brothers were Kui and Gan; his half-brothers were Chongyi, Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo.

sentences.zh: 崇龜，乾寧中廣南節度使；

translations.literal: Chonggui, during Qianning was Military Commissioner of Guangnan;
translations.idiomatic: Chonggui served as military commissioner of Guangnan during Qianning;

sentences.zh: 崇望，乾寧中宰相；

translations.literal: Chongwang, during Qianning was chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: Chongwang was chief minister in the same era;

sentences.zh: 崇魯、崇謨、崇夷，並曆朝省。

translations.literal: Chonglu, Chongmo, and Chongyi all successively served in the central ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Chonglu, Chongmo, and Chongyi all held posts in the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 嶽少孤，亦進士擢第，曆戶部巡官、鄭縣簿、直史館，轉左拾遺、侍御史。

translations.literal: Yue was orphaned young; he also passed the jinshi examination, successively served as touring official of the Ministry of Revenue, registrar of Zheng County, and direct historian of the History Office, and was transferred to Left Reminder and Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Yue also earned his jinshi degree and served in succession as a touring official in the Ministry of Revenue, registrar of Zheng County, and direct historian in the History Office, then as left remonstrance official and attending censor.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明初，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang Zhenming he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as academician.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang Zhenming he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as an academician.

sentences.zh: 嶽為文敏速，尤善談諧，在職累遷戶部侍郎，在翰林十二年。

translations.literal: Yue wrote with quick facility and was especially skilled at witty conversation; in office he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, and served in the Hanlin for twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: Yue wrote with quick facility and had a gift for witty conversation. He rose to vice minister of revenue and spent twelve years in the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，隨例貶均州司馬，尋丁母憂，許自貶所奔喪，服闋，授太子詹事。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, following precedent he was demoted to Defender of Junzhou; soon he entered mourning for his mother, was permitted to rush home for the funeral from his place of demotion, and after the mourning period was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Yue was demoted under the usual purge to defender of Junzhou. He soon entered mourning for his mother and was allowed to leave his post of exile for the funeral; when the mourning ended he was appointed grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，曆兵部吏部侍郎、秘書監、太常卿。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he successively served as Vice Minister of War, Vice Minister of Personnel, Director of the Palace Library, and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he served in succession as vice minister of war, vice minister of personnel, director of the Palace Library, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十六。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 岳文學之外，通於典禮。

translations.literal: Beyond his literary learning, Yue was versed in ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from his literary gifts, Yue was deeply versed in ritual protocol.

sentences.zh: 天成中，奉詔撰《新書儀》一部，文約而理當，今行於世。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng, by imperial order he compiled one work, New Book of Ritual, concise in text and correct in principle, which circulates in the world today.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he was ordered to compile the New Book of Ritual — concise in wording and sound in principle — which remains in use today.

sentences.zh: 子溫叟，仕至御史中丞。

translations.literal: His son Wensou served up to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wensou rose to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 〈（《國老談苑》云：劉溫叟方正守道，以名教為己任。

translations.literal: (Statesmen's Garden of Talk says: Liu Wensou was upright and upheld the Way, taking name and teaching as his personal charge.
translations.idiomatic: (The Statesmen's Garden of Talk records that Liu Wensou was upright and principled, holding himself to the standards of proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事母以孝聞，其母甚賢。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was known for filial service to his mother; his mother was very worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, he was famed for filial devotion to his mother, who was a woman of exceptional virtue.

sentences.zh: 初為翰林學士，私庭拜母，母即命二婢箱擎公服、金帶，置於階下，謂溫叟曰：「此汝父長興中入翰林時所賜也。

translations.literal: When he first became Hanlin academician, in the private courtyard he bowed to his mother; his mother immediately ordered two maidservants to carry in chests the official robes and gold belt, and set them on the steps below, saying to Wensou: "These were bestowed when your father entered the Hanlin in the Changxing era.
translations.idiomatic: When he first became a Hanlin academician, he bowed to his mother in their private courtyard. She at once had two maidservants bring out chests holding official robes and a gold belt and set them on the steps, saying, "These were granted when your father entered the Hanlin in the Changxing era.

sentences.zh: 自先君子薨背以來，嘗懼家門替墜，今汝能自致青雲，繼父之職，可服之無愧矣！」

translations.literal: Since your late father's passing I have feared the family's decline; now you can reach the blue clouds on your own, succeeding to your father's office — you may wear them without shame!"
translations.idiomatic: Since your father's death I have feared our house would fall into decline. Now you have risen on your own merits to succeed to his post — wear them without shame!"

sentences.zh: 因欷歔掩泣。

translations.literal: Thereupon she sighed and sobbed, covering her face with tears.
translations.idiomatic: With that she sighed and wept, covering her face.

sentences.zh: 溫叟伏地號慟，退就別寢，素衣蔬食，追慕數日，然後服之，士大夫以為得禮。）〉

translations.literal: Wensou prostrated himself and wailed loudly; he withdrew to a separate chamber, wore plain clothes and ate simple food, mourned in remembrance for several days, and only then donned the robes — the gentry considered this proper ritual.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Wensou prostrated himself and wailed aloud, then withdrew to another room, dressed in plain clothes and ate simple fare, and mourned his father for several days before putting on the robes. Men of cultivation held this to be proper ritual.)〉

sentences.zh: 封舜卿，

translations.literal: Feng Shunqing,
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shunqing,

sentences.zh: 〈（案：原本有闕文。

translations.idiomatic: (The received text is defective here.

sentences.zh: 據《新唐書·宰相世係表》，封氏世居渤海蓚縣。

translations.literal: According to the New Book of Tang, Genealogical Tables of Chief Ministers, the Feng clan for generations dwelt in Raoyang County, Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: According to the New Book of Tang's tables of chief ministers, the Feng clan had long resided in Raoyang County in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 舜卿，字讚聖，父敖，字碩夫，戶部尚書、渤海縣男。

translations.literal: Shunqing, style name Zansheng; his father Ao, style name Shuofu, was Minister of Revenue and Baron of Bohai County.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqing's style was Zansheng. His father Ao, style Shuofu, had been minister of revenue and Baron of Bohai County.

sentences.zh: 《唐書》有傳。）〉

translations.literal: The Book of Tang has his biography.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Tang contains his biography.)〉

sentences.zh: 仕梁，為禮部侍郎，知貢舉。

translations.literal: Serving the Liang, he was Vice Minister of Rites and oversaw the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he served as vice minister of rites and supervised the civil-service examinations.

sentences.zh: 開平三年，奉使幽州，以門生鄭致雍從行，復命之日，又與致雍同受命入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiping, on a mission to Youzhou, he took his student Zheng Zhiyong to accompany him; on the day of reporting back, both he and Zhiyong received orders to enter the Hanlin as academicians.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 3 (909) he was sent on a mission to Youzhou with his protégé Zheng Zhiyong as companion. On the day he reported back, both men were appointed Hanlin academicians.

sentences.zh: 致雍有俊才，舜卿雖有文辭，才思拙澀，及試五題，不勝困弊，因托致雍秉筆，當時譏者以為座主辱門生。

translations.literal: Zhiyong had brilliant talent; although Shunqing had literary polish, his creative thought was clumsy and slow, and when tested on five topics he could not bear the strain, so he entrusted Zhiyong to wield the brush — contemporaries mocked this as the examination patron shaming his student.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyong was brilliantly gifted. Shunqing had literary polish but slow, labored invention; when tested on five topics he was overwhelmed and asked Zhiyong to draft for him — contemporaries mocked it as a patron disgracing his protégé.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉

translations.idiomatic: (The text is defective from this point.)〉

sentences.zh: 莊宗同光已來，累曆清顯。

translations.literal: From Zhuangzong's Tongguang onward, he successively held pure and eminent offices.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhuangzong's Tongguang era onward he held a series of high, prestigious posts.

sentences.zh: 封氏自太和以來，世居兩製，以文筆稱於時。

translations.literal: The Feng clan from the Taihe era onward for generations held the two drafting posts, renowned in their time for literary brushwork.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Taihe era the Feng family had for generations held the two chief drafting posts and were famed for their literary skill.

sentences.zh: 舜卿從子渭，

translations.literal: Shunqing's nephew Wei,
translations.idiomatic: Shunqing's nephew Wei,

sentences.zh: 〈（《世係表》：渭，字希叟。）〉

translations.literal: (Genealogical Tables: Wei, style name Xisou.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The genealogical tables give his style as Xisou.)〉

sentences.zh: 昭宗遷洛時，為翰林學士，舜卿為中書舍人，叔侄對掌內外製。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, he was Hanlin academician while Shunqing was Secretariat Drafting Secretary — uncle and nephew jointly held inner and outer drafting.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Wei was a Hanlin academician while Shunqing was a Secretariat drafting secretary — uncle and nephew together controlled inner and outer edict drafting.

sentences.zh: 從子翹，於梁貞明中亦為翰林學士。

translations.literal: His nephew Qiao, during Liang Zhenming also became Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Qiao likewise became a Hanlin academician during Liang Zhenming.

sentences.zh: 天成中，為給事中，因轉對上言，以星辰合度，風雨應時，請御前香一合，帝親爇一炷，餘令於塔廟中焚之，貴表精至。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng he was Supervising Censor; in a rotating audience memorial he stated that the stars and planets were in accord and wind and rain came in season, requesting one measure of incense before the throne — the emperor personally burned one stick, and ordered the remainder burned at pagodas and temples, showing precious sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he served as supervising censor. In a rotating audience he reported that the heavens and seasons were in harmony and asked for incense before the throne. The emperor burned one stick himself and had the rest offered at pagodas and temples — a gesture of rare devotion.

sentences.zh: 議者以翹時推名族，出朝苑，登瑣闈，甚有岩廊之望，而忽有此請，乃近諸妖佞耳，物望由是減之。

translations.literal: Commentators held that Qiao was then esteemed as a great-clan figure who had left the court garden and ascended the privy gate, with great prospects for the state council — yet suddenly making such a request was close to the ways of sorcerers and flatterers, and public esteem for him diminished accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Qiao, a man of eminent lineage who had risen from the Hanlin to high office with every prospect of reaching the chief councils, had suddenly made a request fit for sorcerers and sycophants — and his reputation never recovered.

sentences.zh: 竇夢徵，同州人。

translations.literal: Dou Mengzheng was a native of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Mengzheng was a native of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 少苦心為文，登進士第，曆校書郎，自拾遺召入翰林，充學士。

translations.literal: In youth he labored at writing, passed the jinshi examination, successively served as proofreader, and from Reminder was summoned into the Hanlin to serve as academician.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to letters from youth, passed the jinshi examination, served as proofreader, and was summoned from the remonstrance post into the Hanlin as an academician.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，加兩浙錢鏐元帥之命。

translations.literal: During Liang Zhenming, the commission of Grand Marshal was conferred on Qian Liu of the two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: During Liang Zhenming the court issued an edict making Qian Liu of the two Zhe circuits grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 夢徵以鏐無功於中原，兵柄不宜虛授，其言切直。

translations.literal: Mengzheng held that Liu had rendered no service to the central plains and that military authority ought not be granted in vain; his words were sharp and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Mengzheng argued that Liu had done nothing for the central realm and that military command should not be handed out lightly. His memorial was blunt and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝以觸時忌，左授外任。

translations.literal: The Last Liang Emperor, because he had touched a taboo of the times, demoted him to an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Liang Emperor, offended by his candor, demoted him to a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》：竇以錢公無功於本朝，僻在一方，坐邀恩澤，不稱是命，乃抱麻哭於朝。

translations.literal: (Jade Hall Idle Talk: Dou held that Lord Qian had rendered no service to the dynasty, dwelt remote in one region, and yet sat receiving grace — the commission did not fit; he therefore embraced the hemp mourning garb and wept at court.
translations.idiomatic: (Jade Hall Idle Talk records that Dou argued Lord Qian had done nothing for the dynasty yet sat in a remote corner receiving favors unearned by merit. Deeming the commission unfitting, he embraced the mourning hemp and wept in open court.

sentences.zh: 翌日，竇謫掾於東州。）〉

translations.literal: The next day Dou was banished as an aide in an eastern prefecture.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The next day Dou was banished to serve as an aide in an eastern prefecture.)〉

sentences.zh: 有頃，復召為學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was again summoned as academician.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗入汴，夢徵以例貶沂州，居嘗感梁末帝舊恩，因為《祭故君文》云：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Mengzheng was demoted under precedent to Yizhou; dwelling there he often felt the old grace of the Last Liang Emperor, and therefore composed A Eulogy for the Former Lord, saying: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Mengzheng was demoted under the usual purge to Yizhou. Grateful still for the Last Liang Emperor's past kindness, he wrote A Eulogy for the Former Lord, which begins: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 四海九州，天回眷命，一女二夫，人之不幸。

translations.literal: Within the four seas and nine provinces, Heaven turns its favor — one woman, two husbands: man's misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Across the realm Heaven has shifted its mandate — like one woman with two husbands, a thing no loyal subject can bear without grief.

sentences.zh: 當革故以鼎新，若金銷而火盛，必然之理，夫何足競」云。

translations.literal: When the old must be changed for the new, as metal melts and fire blazes — the necessary principle — what is there to contend over," and so on.
translations.idiomatic: When the old must give way to the new, as metal melts in a raging fire — such is necessity; what is there to struggle against?" and so forth.

sentences.zh: 秉筆者皆許之，尋量移宿州。

translations.literal: The drafters all praised it; soon he was transferred on reduced penalty to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow writers praised the piece, and he was soon transferred on reduced penalty to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 天成初，遷中書舍人，復入為翰林學士、工部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Secretary, again entered service as Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he was made a Secretariat drafting secretary, then again entered the Hanlin and rose to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously ennobled as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》：竇失意被謫，嘗鬱鬱不樂，曾夢有人謂曰：「君無自苦，不久當復故職。

translations.literal: (Jade Hall Idle Talk: Dou, disheartened in banishment, was often depressed; once he dreamed someone said: "Do not torment yourself — before long you will return to your former office.
translations.idiomatic: (Jade Hall Idle Talk adds that Dou, disheartened in exile, grew despondent. In a dream someone told him, "Do not torment yourself — you will soon return to your former post.

sentences.zh: 然將來慎勿為丞相，苟有是命，當萬計避之。」

translations.literal: Yet in the future be careful never to become chief minister; if such a command should come, you must by every means avoid it."
translations.idiomatic: But hereafter beware of becoming chief minister. If such an appointment should come, avoid it by every means you can."

sentences.zh: 其後竇復居禁職。

translations.literal: Afterward Dou again held a forbidden-office post.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to a palace post.

sentences.zh: 有頃，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 竇忽憶夢中所言，深惡其事。

translations.literal: Dou suddenly recalled what was said in the dream and deeply dreaded that matter.
translations.idiomatic: Dou suddenly remembered the dream and dreaded what it foretold.

sentences.zh: 然已受命，不能遜避，未幾果卒。）〉

translations.literal: Yet he had already received the command and could not decline; before long he indeed died.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had already accepted the appointment and could not refuse. Before long he died, just as the dream had warned.)〉

sentences.zh: 夢徵隨計之秋，文稱甚高，尤長於箋啟，編為十卷，目曰《東堂集》，行於世。

translations.literal: In the autumn of Mengzheng's examination journey his writing was greatly acclaimed; he was especially skilled at letters and memorials, compiled in ten fascicles under the title Eastern Hall Collection, circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of his civil-service examination his writing won high praise. He excelled especially at letters and memorials, which were collected in ten fascicles as Eastern Hall Collection and circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 李保殷，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Baoyin was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyin was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 昭宗朝，自處士除太子正字，改錢塘縣尉。

translations.literal: During Zhaozong's reign, from Recluse Scholar he was appointed Proofreader of the Heir Apparent, then changed to Magistrate of Qiantang County.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaozong he rose from recluse scholar to proofreader of the heir apparent, then became magistrate of Qiantang County.

sentences.zh: 浙東帥董昌辟為推官，調補河府兵曹參軍，曆長水令、《毛詩》博士，累官至太常少卿、端王傅。

translations.literal: The Zhedong military commissioner Dong Chang recruited him as investigating officer; he was transferred to fill a post as military staff officer of the He prefecture, successively served as Magistrate of Changshui and Doctor of the Mao Odes, and rose to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with junior third rank and Tutor of the Prince of Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang, military commissioner of eastern Zhe, recruited him as investigating officer. He was transferred to a staff post in the He prefecture, served as magistrate of Changshui and doctor of the Mao Odes, and rose to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and tutor to the Prince of Duan.

sentences.zh: 入為大理卿，撰《刑律總要》十二卷；

translations.literal: He entered service as Director of the Court of Judicial Review and compiled Essentials of Penal Statutes in twelve fascicles;
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as director of the Court of Judicial Review and compiled Essentials of Penal Statutes in twelve fascicles;

sentences.zh: 與兵部侍郎郗殷象論刑法事。

translations.literal: and with Vice Minister of War Xi Yinxiang discussed matters of penal law.
translations.idiomatic: and discussed penal law with Vice Minister of War Xi Yinxiang.

sentences.zh: 左降房州司馬。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Defender of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to defender of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 同光初，授殿中監，以其素有明法律之譽，拜大理卿；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was appointed Director of the Palace Domestic Service; because he had long enjoyed a reputation for mastery of law, he was appointed Director of Judicial Review;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang he was made director of the palace domestic service and, on his long-standing reputation for legal expertise, was appointed director of judicial review;

sentences.zh: 未滿秩，屬為人所製。

translations.literal: before his term was complete, he happened to be framed by others.
translations.idiomatic: but before his term ended he was framed by enemies.

sentences.zh: 保殷曰：「人之多辟，無自立辟。」

translations.literal: Baoyin said: "When many people commit offenses, do not create offenses for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin said, "When the world is full of crime, do not make yourself a criminal."

sentences.zh: 乃謝病以歸，卒於洛陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pleaded illness and returned home, dying in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and retired to Luoyang, where he died.

sentences.zh: 歸藹，字文彥，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Gui Ai, style name Wenyan, was a native of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Ai, whose style was Wenyan, was a native of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖登，祖融，父仁澤，位皆至列曹尚書、觀察使。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Deng, grandfather Rong, and father Renze all rose to the posts of ranking secretary in the boards and military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Deng, grandfather Rong, and father Renze all rose to ranking secretariat posts and military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 藹登進士第，及升朝，遍曆三署。

translations.literal: Ai passed the jinshi examination; when he entered court service he served in turn in all three secretariat offices.
translations.idiomatic: Ai passed the jinshi examination and, once he entered court service, served in turn in all three secretariat offices.

sentences.zh: 據《舊唐書·昭宗紀》：天祐元年七月，宴於文思殿。

translations.literal: According to the Annals of Zhaozong in the Old Book of Tang: In the seventh month of the first year of Tianyou, a banquet was held in the Wensi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Annals of Zhaozong in the Old Book of Tang, in the seventh month of Tianyou 1 (904) a banquet was held in Wensi Hall.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠入，百官或坐於廊下，全忠怒，笞通引官何凝。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong entered; some of the hundred officials were seated in the corridor below, and Quanzhong was angered and had the usher He Ning flogged.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong entered, some officials were seated in the corridor below. Quanzhong was enraged and had the usher He Ning flogged.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，製金紫光祿大夫、行御史中丞、上柱國韓儀責授棣州司馬，侍御史歸藹責授登州司戶，坐百官傲全忠也。）

translations.literal: On bingyin, an edict demoted Grand Master of the Golden Glow and Purple Ornament, Acting Censor, and Supreme Pillar of State Han Yi to defender of Dizhou, and Remonstrating Censor Gui Ai to registrar of Dengzhou—for the offense of the hundred officials' arrogance toward Quanzhong.)
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin an edict demoted Han Yi, grand master of the golden glow and purple ornament, acting censor, and supreme pillar of state, to defender of Dizhou, and remonstrating censor Gui Ai to registrar of Dengzhou, for the offense of officials' arrogance toward Quanzhong.)

sentences.zh: 同光初，為尚書右丞，遷刑、戶二部侍郎，以太子賓客致仕，卒年七十六。

translations.literal: Early in Tongguang he served as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to vice minister of punishments and households, retired as Honorary Attendant to the Crown Prince, and died at seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang he served as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to vice minister of punishments and households, retired as honorary attendant to the crown prince, and died at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 孔邈，文宣王四十一代孫。

translations.literal: Kong Miao was a forty-first-generation descendant of the Cultured Propagator King.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Miao was a forty-first-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺餘，神氣溫厚。

translations.literal: His body was over seven chi in height; his spirit and bearing were warm and substantial.
translations.idiomatic: He stood over seven chi tall, with a warm and dignified bearing.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，曆校書郎、萬年尉，充集賢校理，為諫議大夫，以年老致仕。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, successively served as proofreader and Wannian district defender, acted as collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, became Grand Censor, and retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as proofreader, defender of Wannian district, and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies before becoming grand censor and retiring on account of age.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：《孔邈傳》，原本殘闕。

translations.literal: (Note: the Biography of Kong Miao in the original is defective.
translations.idiomatic: (The received Biography of Kong Miao is defective.

sentences.zh: 考《冊府元龜》云：乾寧五年，登進士第，除校書郎。

translations.literal: Examining the Prime Tortoise of the Archives of the Realm, it states: In the fifth year of Qianning he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: The Prime Tortoise of the Archives of the Realm records that in Qianning 5 (898) he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed proofreader.

sentences.zh: 崔遠在中書，奏為萬年尉，充集賢校理，以親舅獨孤損方在廊廟，避嫌不赴職。）〉

translations.literal: Cui Yuan was in the Secretariat and memorialized appointing him Wannian defender and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; because his maternal uncle Dugu Sun was then in the state council, he avoided suspicion and did not take up the post.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan, then in the Secretariat, recommended him as defender of Wannian and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, but Miao declined the posts because his maternal uncle Dugu Sun was serving in the chief councils and he wished to avoid suspicion.)〉

sentences.zh: 張文寶，昭宗朝諫議大夫顗之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenbao was the son of Grand Censor Yi of Zhaozong's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenbao was the son of Grand Censor Yi, who had served under Emperor Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 文寶初，依河中朱友謙為從事。

translations.literal: Early in Wenbao's career he relied on Zhu Youqian of Hezhong as staff member.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career Wenbao served on the staff of Zhu Youqian in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位於魏州，以文寶知制誥，曆中書舍人、刑部侍郎、左散騎常侍、知貢舉，遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Wenbao was made Drafting Commissioner, successively served as Secretariat Drafting Secretary, Vice Minister of Punishments, Left Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and overseer of examinations, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Wenbao was made drafting commissioner and rose through the posts of Secretariat drafting secretary, vice minister of punishments, left honorary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and examination supervisor before becoming vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 文寶性雅淡稽古。

translations.literal: Wenbao's nature was refined, restrained, and devoted to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbao was refined, reserved, and devoted to classical learning.

sentences.zh: 長興初，奉使浙中，泛海船壞，水工以小舟救，文寶與副使吏部郎中張絢信風至淮南界，偽吳楊溥禮待甚至，兼厚遺錢幣、食物。

translations.literal: Early in Changxing, on a mission to Zhe, his seagoing vessel was wrecked; sailors rescued them in small boats. Wenbao and the vice-envoy, Personnel Bureau Director Zhang Xuan, trusted the wind and reached the Huainan border; the false Wu ruler Yang Pu received them with extreme courtesy and also gave generous gifts of money and food.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changxing, on a mission to Zhe, his ship was wrecked at sea and sailors rescued him and his party in small boats. Wenbao and his deputy, Personnel Bureau director Zhang Xuan, drifted on the wind to the Huainan border, where Yang Pu of Wu received them with exceptional courtesy and lavished money and provisions on them.

sentences.zh: 文寶受其食物，反其錢幣，吳人善之，送文寶等復至杭州宣國命，還青州，卒。

translations.literal: Wenbao accepted their food but returned their money; the Wu people approved, sent Wenbao and the others back to Hangzhou to announce the imperial command, returned to Qingzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbao accepted the food but returned the money, which won the Wu people's admiration. They escorted him back to Hangzhou to deliver the imperial commission, then he returned to Qingzhou and died.

sentences.zh: 子吉，嗣位邑宰。

translations.literal: His son Ji succeeded to the district magistracy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji succeeded to his father's district magistracy.

sentences.zh: 陳乂，薊門人也。

translations.literal: Chen Yi was a man of Jimen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi was a native of Jimen.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 因避亂，客於浮陽，轉徙於大梁。

translations.literal: To escape the turmoil he stayed as a guest in Fuyang and then moved to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: To escape the turmoil he lived as a guest in Fuyang and then moved to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 梁將張漢傑延於私邸，表授太子舍人。

translations.literal: The Liang general Zhang Hanjie invited him to his private residence and memorialized his appointment as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang general Zhang Hanjie invited him to his private residence and memorialized his appointment as attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平梁，郭崇韜遙領常山，召居賓榻。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Guo Chongtao held distant charge of Changshan and summoned him to his guest couch.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Guo Chongtao held distant charge of Changshan and summoned him to his guest couch.

sentences.zh: 崇韜從魏王繼岌伐蜀，署為招討判官。

translations.literal: When Chongtao followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in the campaign against Shu, he appointed him pacification commissioner-assessor.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongtao followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in the campaign against Shu, he appointed him pacification commissioner-assessor.

sentences.zh: 崇韜死，明宗即位，隨任圜歸闕，圜薦之於朝，除膳部員外郎、知制誥，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: After Chongtao died and Mingzong took the throne, he followed Ren Yuan back to court; Yuan recommended him to the court, and he was appointed Vice Director of the Board of Provisions and Drafting Commissioner, then successively promoted to Secretariat Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongtao died and Mingzong took the throne, he followed Ren Yuan back to court. Yuan recommended him, and he was appointed vice director of the Board of Provisions and drafting commissioner, then rose to Secretariat drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 乂性陰僻，寡與人合，不為當路所與。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was dark and withdrawn; he seldom got along with others and was not favored by those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was secretive and withdrawn, seldom got along with others, and was not favored by those in power.

sentences.zh: 尋移左散騎常侍，由是忿以成疾，逾月而卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; thereby resentment became illness, and after more than a month he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to left honorary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary. Resentment turned to illness, and after more than a month he died.

sentences.zh: 乂微有才術，嘗自恃其能。

translations.literal: Yi had modest talent and skill and once relied on his own ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had modest talent and once relied heavily on his own ability.

sentences.zh: 為判官日，人有造者，垂帷深處，罕見其面。

translations.literal: When he was an assessor, if someone came to visit him he would hang curtains deep within and rarely show his face.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as an assessor, when visitors came he hung curtains deep within and rarely showed his face.

sentences.zh: 及居西掖，而姿態愈倨，位竟不至公卿，蓋器度促狹者也。

translations.literal: When he held office in the western secretariat his bearing became all the more haughty; in the end his rank never reached the highest offices—likely because his capacity was narrow and cramped.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held office in the western secretariat his bearing grew all the more haughty. In the end his rank never reached the highest offices—likely because his capacity was narrow.

sentences.zh: 然乂性孤執，尤廉於財。

translations.literal: Yet Yi's nature was solitary and stubborn, and he was especially scrupulous about money.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yi was solitary and stubborn and especially scrupulous about money.

sentences.zh: 長興中，嘗自舍人銜命冊晉國公主石氏於太原，晉高祖善待之，但訝其高岸。

translations.literal: During Changxing, as drafting secretary he carried orders to invest Princess Shi of the Jin state at Taiyuan; the Gaozu of Jin treated him well but was surprised at his lofty and stern bearing.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing, as drafting secretary he carried orders to invest Princess Shi of Jin at Taiyuan. The Gaozu of Jin treated him well but was surprised at his lofty and stern bearing.

sentences.zh: 人或有獻可於乂，宜陳一謳頌以稱晉高祖之美，可邀其厚賄耳。

translations.literal: Some advised Yi that he should present a eulogy praising the beauty of the Gaozu of Jin and thereby win a generous reward.
translations.idiomatic: Some advised Yi to present a eulogy praising the Gaozu of Jin and thereby win a generous reward.

sentences.zh: 乂曰：「人生貧富，咸有定分，未有持天子命違禮以求利，既損國綱，且虧士行，乂今生所不為也。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "Whether one's life is poor or rich has its fixed allotment; there has never been one who held Heaven's Son's command yet violated ritual to seek profit—this harms the state's norms and moreover shames the scholar's conduct; this is something Yi will never do in this life."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Whether life is poor or rich has its fixed allotment. No one who bears Heaven's Son's command should violate ritual to seek profit—this harms the state's norms and shames a scholar's conduct. That is something I will never do in this life."

sentences.zh: 聞者嘉之。

translations.literal: Those who heard praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard praised him.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖即位，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu of Jin took the throne, he was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu of Jin took the throne, Yi was posthumously awarded minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 劉讚，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zan was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zan was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼有文性。

translations.literal: In youth he had literary aptitude.
translations.idiomatic: He showed literary promise from childhood.

sentences.zh: 父比，為令錄，誨以詩書，夏月令服青襦單衫。

translations.literal: His father Bi served as county recorder; he instructed him with poetry and books, and in summer months ordered him to wear a blue jacket and single-layer shirt.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bi was a county recorder who taught him the classics and, in summer, made him wear only a plain blue jacket and single-layer shirt.

sentences.zh: 比每肉食，別置蔬食以飯讚，謂之曰：「肉食，君之祿也。

translations.literal: Whenever Bi ate meat, he set aside vegetable food to feed Zan, saying to him: "Meat is the ruler's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Bi ate meat he set vegetables before Zan and said, "Meat is an official's perquisite.

sentences.zh: 爾欲食肉，當苦心文藝，自可致之，吾祿不可分也。」

translations.literal: If you wish to eat meat, you must labor at literary arts — you can obtain it yourself; my salary cannot be shared."
translations.idiomatic: If you want meat, earn it through your own literary merit. I cannot share my salary with you."

sentences.zh: 由是讚及冠有文辭，年三十餘登進士第。

translations.literal: From this Zan by the capping age had literary compositions; in his thirties he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zan grew into a polished writer and passed the jinshi examination in his thirties.

sentences.zh: 魏州節度使羅紹威署巡官，罷歸京師，依開封尹劉鄩。

translations.literal: Weizhou Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei appointed him touring officer; when dismissed he returned to the capital and relied on Kaifeng Prefect Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei, military commissioner of Weizhou, appointed him touring officer. When that post ended he went to the capital and attached himself to Kaifeng prefect Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 久之，租庸使趙岩表為巡官，累遷至戶部員外郎，職如故。

translations.literal: After a long time, Grain-Tax Commissioner Zhao Yan memorialized him as touring officer; he was repeatedly promoted to Outer Court Director of the Ministry of Revenue, his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Grain-Tax Commissioner Zhao Yan recommended him as touring officer, and he rose to outer-court director in the Ministry of Revenue while keeping the same duties.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，租庸副使孔謙以讚里人，表為鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Deputy Grain-Tax Commissioner Kong Qian, as Zan's fellow townsman, memorialized him as Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Deputy Grain-Tax Commissioner Kong Qian, a fellow townsman, recommended Zan as salt and iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天成中，曆知制誥、中書舍人。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng he successively served as Drafting Commissioner and Secretariat Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he served in succession as drafting commissioner and Secretariat drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 與學士竇夢徵同年登第，鄰居友善，夢徵卒，讚與同年楊凝式緦麻為位而哭，其家無嫡長，與視喪事，恤其孀稚，人士稱之。

translations.literal: With academician Dou Mengzheng he had passed the examination in the same year and were friendly neighbors; when Mengzheng died, Zan with his year-mate Yang Ningshi wore hemp mourning and set up a mourning place to weep; the family had no eldest legitimate son — he assisted in overseeing the funeral, comforted the widow and young, and men of cultivation praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the jinshi in the same year as Hanlin academician Dou Mengzheng, and they were friendly neighbors. When Mengzheng died, Zan and his year-mate Yang Ningshi donned hemp mourning and wept at the bier. The family had no eldest son, so Zan helped manage the funeral and cared for the widow and children — conduct widely praised.

sentences.zh: 改御史中丞、刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was made censor-in-chief and vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 讚性雍和，與物無忤，居官畏慎，人若以私幹之，雖權豪不能移其操。

translations.literal: Zan's nature was mild and harmonious; he did not clash with others; in office he was cautious and fearful of error — if people tried to approach him with private requests, even powerful families could not shift his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was gentle and easy in manner, careful in office, and immovable in principle — even the powerful could not sway him with private appeals.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改秘書監，兼秦王傅。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Director of the Palace Library, concurrently Tutor of the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made director of the Palace Library and tutor to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 〈（《冊府元龜》：秦王為元帥，秦王府判官、太子詹事王居敏與讚鄉曲之舊，以秦王盛年自恣，須朝中選端士納誨，冀其稟畏，乃奏薦讚焉。）〉

translations.literal: (Prime Tortoise: The Prince of Qin was Grand Marshal; Qin Prince's Mansion judge and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Wang Jumin was an old fellow townsman of Zan; because the Prince of Qin in his prime was self-indulgent, upright scholars from court needed to be selected to offer admonition, hoping he would receive and fear them — therefore he memorialized recommending Zan.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Prime Tortoise records that when the Prince of Qin was grand marshal, Wang Jumin, judge of the Qin princely mansion and grand mentor of the heir apparent, an old fellow townsman of Zan, recommended him because the young prince was self-indulgent and needed upright court scholars to admonish him.)〉

sentences.zh: 讚節概貞素，忽聞其命，掩泣固辭，竟不能止。

translations.literal: Zan was upright and plain in integrity; suddenly hearing this appointment, he covered his face weeping and firmly declined, but in the end could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A man of plain integrity, Zan wept and firmly declined when he heard of the appointment, but could not refuse it.

sentences.zh: 〈（案《通鑒》：瓚自以左遷，泣訴，不得免。

translations.literal: (Examining the Comprehensive Mirror: Zan regarded it as a demotion, wept and pleaded, and could not be excused.
translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian records that Zan regarded the appointment as a demotion, wept and pleaded, and could not be excused.

sentences.zh: 胡三省注云：唐制，六部侍郎除吏部之外，餘皆從四品下；

translations.literal: Hu Sanxing's note states: Under Tang regulations, vice ministers of the six ministries except Personnel were all junior fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sanxing notes that under Tang regulations, vice ministers of the six ministries except Personnel were junior fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 王傅從三品。

translations.literal: princely tutors were junior third rank.
translations.idiomatic: while princely tutors were junior third rank.

sentences.zh: 然六部侍郎為向用，王傅為左遷，以職事有閑劇之不同也。

translations.literal: Yet vice ministers of the six ministries were posts for advancement, while princely tutors were a demotion — because duties differed in leisure and urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a vice ministry post was a stepping stone to higher office, while a princely tutorship was effectively a demotion, because the duties differed in prestige and influence.

sentences.zh: 當是時，從榮地居儲副，則秦王傅不可以閑官。

translations.literal: At that time Congrong's position was as heir apparent, so the Prince of Qin's tutor could not be an idle office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Congrong held the position of heir apparent, so the Prince of Qin's tutor was no sinecure.

sentences.zh: 言蓋以從榮輕佻峻急，恐豫其禍，故求脫耳。）〉

translations.literal: The words likely meant that because Congrong was frivolous, sharp, and harsh, he feared sharing in his calamity and therefore sought to escape.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The comment suggests Zan feared Congrong's rash and violent character and sought to escape before disaster struck.)〉

sentences.zh: 時秦王參佐，皆新進小生，動多輕脫，每稱頌秦王功德，阿意順旨，隻奉談笑，惟讚從容諷議，必獻嘉言。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Qin's staff were all newly risen young men, often frivolous; they constantly praised the prince's merit and virtue, flattered his intent, and attended only to banter — only Zan with composure offered indirect admonition and always presented good counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's staff were young upstarts, frivolous and eager to flatter. They praised his virtues and joined his revels — only Zan spoke with measured admonition and offered sound counsel.

sentences.zh: 秦王常接見賓僚及遊客，於酒筵之中，悉令秉筆賦詩。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin often received guests, staff, and traveling scholars; amid wine banquets he ordered all to take brush and compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: The prince often entertained guests and wandering scholars at banquets and required everyone present to compose poetry on the spot.

sentences.zh: 〈（《冊府元龜》：時從榮溺於篇章，凡門客及通謁遊士，必坐於客次，自出題目，令賦一章，然後接見。）〉

translations.literal: (Prime Tortoise: At the time Congrong was addicted to literary compositions; all retainers and visiting scholars seeking audience had to sit in the guest wing — he himself set the topic and ordered one rhapsody composed, and only then received them in audience.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Prime Tortoise adds that Congrong was obsessed with verse. Every retainer and visiting scholar had to wait in the antechamber, compose a poem on a topic the prince set, and only then be received.)〉

sentences.zh: 讚為師傅，亦與諸客混，然容狀不悅。

translations.literal: Zan as tutor was also lumped with the other guests, yet his expression was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: As tutor, Zan was lumped in with the other guests, and his displeasure showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 秦王知其意，自是戒典客，讚至勿通，令每月一度至衙。

translations.literal: The prince knew his mind; from then on he warned the reception officer that when Zan came he was not to be admitted, ordering him to come to the yamen only once a month.
translations.idiomatic: The prince understood his feelings and ordered the gatekeeper never to admit him except for one monthly visit to the princely headquarters.

sentences.zh: 〈（《言行龜鑒》載：劉讚諫秦王曰：「殿下宜以孝敬為職，浮華非所尚也。」

translations.literal: (Mirror of Words and Conduct records: Liu Zan admonished the Prince of Qin: "Your Highness ought to take filial piety and respect as your duty; frivolity is not what should be esteemed."
translations.idiomatic: (The Mirror of Words and Conduct records that Zan admonished the prince: "Your Highness should devote yourself to filial piety and duty. Frivolity is not becoming."

sentences.zh: 秦王不悅，戒閽者後弗引進。）〉

translations.literal: The prince was displeased and warned the gatekeepers thereafter not to admit him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The prince took offense and ordered the gatekeepers never to admit him again.)〉

sentences.zh: 讚既官係王府，不敢朝參，不通慶吊，但閉關喑嗚而已，及秦王得罪，或言讚止於朝降，而讚已服麻衣備驢乘在門矣。

translations.literal: Zan, since his office was tied to the princely mansion, dared not attend court audience, sent no congratulations or condolences, but only shut his door in silent grief; when the prince was condemned, some said Zan would merely submit to court demotion — yet Zan had already donned hemp mourning and prepared donkey and carriage at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Bound to the princely household, Zan stopped attending court or paying social calls and lived in seclusion. When the prince fell, some expected Zan merely to accept demotion — but he had already donned hemp mourning and had a donkey waiting at his gate.

sentences.zh: 聞其言曰：「豈有國君之嗣，一旦舉室塗地，而賓佐朝降，得免死，幸也。」

translations.literal: Hearing this he said: "How can there be an heir of the ruler's house whose whole household is suddenly wiped out, while his staff merely submit to court demotion — to escape death is fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this he said, "When an imperial prince's entire household is destroyed overnight, how can his staff merely accept demotion and call themselves fortunate to escape death?"

sentences.zh: 俄而台史示敕，長流嵐州，即時赴貶所。

translations.literal: Soon the censorate clerk displayed the edict: long exile to Lanzhou — he immediately went to the place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the censorate edict arrived banishing him to Lanzhou, and he set out at once.

sentences.zh: 在嵐州逾年，清泰二年春，詔歸田里。

translations.literal: After more than a year in Lanzhou, in spring of the second year of Qingtai an edict ordered him home to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year in Lanzhou, in spring of Qingtai 2 (935) an edict allowed him to return home.

sentences.zh: 妻紇幹氏塗中卒，讚比羸瘠，慟哭殆絕，因之亦病，行及石會關而卒，時年六十餘。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Heganshi died on the road; Zan was already emaciated, wailed until nearly dead, and thereby also fell ill; traveling as far as Shihui Pass he died, aged over sixty.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Heganshi died on the journey. Already frail, Zan wept until he nearly perished, fell ill himself, and died at Shihui Pass at over sixty years of age.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自唐祚橫流，衣冠掃地，苟無端士，孰恢素風。

translations.literal: The historiographer states: Since the Tang mandate flowed awry and the gentry were swept to the ground, if there were no upright scholars, who could restore the pure wind?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Once the Tang mandate ran awry and the scholar-official class was laid waste, only upright men could restore the old standards.

sentences.zh: 如廷珪之文學，崔沂之剛正，劉嶽之典禮，舜卿之掌誥，洎夢徵而下，皆蔚有貞規，無虧懿範，固可以為搢紳之圭表，聳朝廷之羽儀，以之垂名，夫何不韙。

translations.literal: Such as Tinggui's literary learning, Yi's stern uprightness, Yue's ritual regulations, Shunqing's control of edicts — down to Mengzheng and below — all richly possessed upright norms and did not fall short of fine models; they can indeed serve as standards for the gentry and as feathered banners for the court; to leave their names to posterity — how could that be wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Tinggui in letters, Yi in integrity, Yue in ritual, Shunqing in edict drafting, and from Mengzheng downward all upheld steadfast standards without blemish on their reputations. They may serve as models for the official class and ornaments of the court. To leave such names to posterity — what could be more fitting?
